L0@P0: Funded Study: Safety of B7H3 CAR T cells in Dogs with Spontaneous Cancer
L1@P0: Study Title: Evaluating the safety and immune activities of B7H3 targeting chimeric
L2@P0: antigen receptor T cells in dogs with spontaneous cancer
L3@P0: Purpose of Study:
L4@P0: The purpose of this study is to investigate the safety and activity of genetically-modified
L5@P0: immune cells (specifically chimeric antigen receptor T cells, CAR T cells for short) for
L6@P0: specifically recognizing and eliminating tumor cells that express a specific surface
L7@P0: protein called B7H3 when intravenously infused into pet dogs with spontaneous
L8@P0: cancers.
L9@P0: Inclusion Criteria:
L10@P0: • Dogs with a cytologic or histologic diagnosis of any solid tumor with presumed or
L11@P0: confirmed expression of the B7H3 epitope
L12@P0: • Patient must be in good overall condition
L13@P0: Exclusion Criteria:
L14@P0: • Patient has other serious illness
L15@P0: • Patient has received prior chemotherapy or radiation treatment within 4 weeks of
L16@P0: study enrollment
L17@P0: • Patient is receiving immunosuppressive therapies
L18@P0: Procedures:
L19@P0: Canine patients will receive a series of two chemotherapeutic drugs (fludarabine and
L20@P0: cyclophosphamide) prior to receiving intravenous infusions of genetically-modified,
L21@P0: activated T cells (CAR T cells) following a preset treatment and reevaluation schedule.
L22@P0: During and/or following completion of CAR T cell therapy, blood will be collected for
L23@P0: analysis to confirm successful engraftment of CAR T cells within lymphoid organs and
L24@P0: blood. In addition, tumor tissues might be collected to confirm B7H3 epitope expression,
L25@P0: as well as successful CAR T cell infiltration into tumor tissues.
L26@P0: Compensation:
L27@P0: The study will partially defray costs associated with non-invasive techniques and
L28@P0: radiologic aspects of the project, including blood and radiologic tests, as well as
L29@P0-1: hospitalization required. Possible beneficial effects of this new experimental treatment protocol in canine
L30@P1: oncology patients include the development of a new therapeutic strategy for managing
L31@P1: solid tumors and associated metastatic lesions that express the B7H3 epitope.
L32@P1: Contact Information:
L33@P1: Please feel free to contact our Clinical Trials Coordinator, Rebecca Kamerer, at (217)
L34@P1: 300-6453 or rmoss81@illinois.edu to refer a patient or for any additional information.
L35@P1: Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.
L36@P1: Study Sponsors:
L37@P1: The college gratefully acknowledges funding for this study from GREYLong and Canine
L38@P1: Cancer Alliance.

L72: ## High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for Lymphoma in Dogs
L73: 
L74: ### Principal Investigators
L75: 
L76:   * Dr. Nick Dervisis, Associate Professor, Oncology
L77:   * Dr. Michael Childress, Professor, Comparative Oncology
L78: ### Background
L79: 
L80: Lymphoma is one of the most common cancers in dogs, and while chemotherapy can often put the disease into remission, it is rarely curative. This study is investigating whether a noninvasive technology, High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), can safely destroy part of a cancerous lymph node and stimulate the immune system to help fight the cancer throughout the body.
L81: HIFU uses precisely focused ultrasound energy to generate heat that kills cancer cells within a targeted region, without surgery or radiation. Beyond directly killing tumor cells, this process may release tumor antigens and danger signals, "waking up" the immune system to recognize and attack lymphoma cells wherever they are.
L82: In this trial, we will treat one enlarged lymph node with HIFU in dogs who have not yet received chemotherapy. We will then carefully analyze changes in the treated lymph node, an untreated lymph node, and the blood to see if the immune system is activated. All dogs will then receive a full course of standard CHOP chemotherapy at Purdue.
L83: The potential benefits for participating dogs include receiving an innovative treatment at no cost, which may improve the effectiveness of chemotherapy and potentially help the immune system keep the cancer under control longer. There are no placebos in this trial.
L84: ### Eligibility for Dogs to Participate in the Study
L85:   * Be at least 1 year old and weigh over 8 kg (~18 lb)
L86:   * Have an untreated, newly confirmed diagnosis of intermediate or large-cell, multicentric lymphoma (B or T-cell)
L87:   * Have not received any chemotherapy, corticosteroids, or other anti-cancer treatment in the past 3 weeks (2 weeks for steroids)
L88:   * Be healthy enough for sedation/anesthesia
L89:   * Have completed full clinical staging (physical exam, lab work, imaging, and lymph node biopsy)
L90:   * Have no other serious life-limiting diseases
L91: ### Exclusion Criteria
L92: 
L93:   * Small-cell lymphoma or other round cell tumors
L94:   * Stage V lymphoma (bone marrow or blood involvement) or extranodal lymphoma
L95:   * Significant liver or kidney dysfunction
L96:   * Poor overall performance status (VCOG > 2)
L97: ### What is involved for the dog/dog owner?
L98: 
L99: Screening and Baseline Testing:
L100: 
L101: Owners will first meet with our oncology team to discuss standard treatment options. If interested in the trial, dogs will undergo:
L102: 
L103:   * Physical exam, CBC, chemistry, urinalysis
L104:   * Thoracic radiographs and abdominal ultrasound
L105:   * Lymph node biopsy (histopathology, immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry)
L106:   * Clonality testing (PARR)
L107: 
L108: Study Procedures:
L109:   * Day 0 (Baseline Sampling):
L110:     * Needle biopsy of a lymph node on the opposite side of the biopsied lymph node
L111:     * Blood draw for extracellular vesicle (EV) analysis
L112:   * HIFU Treatment:
L113:     * Within 1-7 days of baseline sampling, a portion of the target lymph node will be thermally ablated using the Theraclion Echopulse HIFU system under sedation.
L114:   * Post-Treatment Sampling:
L115:     * 5-7 days after HIFU: repeat needle biopsies of treated and untreated lymph nodes and blood collection
L116:   * Chemotherapy:
L117:     * CHOP-based UW-25 protocol will begin immediately after post-HIFU sampling and continue for 25 weeks
L118:   * Follow-Up:
L119:     * Regular rechecks during chemotherapy for monitoring bloodwork and treatment response
L120:     * Long-term monitoring until relapse
L121: ### Financial Support
L122: 
L123: Once enrolled, the following will be provided at no cost:
L124: 
L125:   * The HIFU procedure, including sedation/anesthesia
L126:   * All biopsies, blood tests, and lab work required by the study
L127:   * A $2,000 credit toward the cost of the CHOP chemotherapy protocol
L128:   * Up to $2,000 in additional support for managing any side effects linked to HIFU, or to be applied toward CHOP therapy
L129:   * Reduced pricing ("research rate") for all other treatments and follow-up visits
L130: Owners will be responsible for costs related to:
L131: 
L132:   * Initial diagnostic workup prior to enrollment
L133:   * Any unrelated to HIFU medical care
L134:   * Emergency visits due to HIFU outside of Purdue University Veterinary Hospital
L135: ### Trial Status
L136: 
L137:  Currently Enrolling
L138: ### Questions
L139: 
L140: Pet owners and veterinarians interested in this trial should contact the Tumor Ablation Lab.
L141: 
L142: Email:   TumorAblation@purdue.edu
L143: We recommend scheduling an appointment for evaluation with our team, and specifically mention the name of the trial (High Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for Lymphoma in Dogs). The visit will allow us to determine if the trial is the best option for your dog and whether they are eligible or not. If we determine that the trial is not the best option for your pet, we will be happy to assist with other treatments. A written referral from your veterinarian is required to schedule appointment.

L146: ## H-FIRE Liver Cancer Study
L147: 
L148: ### Principal Investigators
L149: 
L150:   * Dr. Nick Dervisis, Associate Professor, Oncology
L151: ### Study Overview
L152: This clinical trial is evaluating the safety and immune effects of High-Frequency Irreversible Electroporation (H-FIRE) for dogs diagnosed with liver cancer. While surgical removal of liver tumors can lead to excellent outcomes in selected cases, dogs with non-resectable or advanced disease currently have very limited treatment options and poor prognosis.
L153: H-FIRE is a novel, image-guided, non-thermal tumor ablation technology that delivers high-frequency electrical pulses to create microscopic pores in cancer cell membranes, leading to tumor cell death and potential immune activation.
L154: ### Purpose of the Study
L155: 
L156: The goals of this study are to evaluate the safety and feasibility of H-FIRE in dogs with liver cancer, measure local and systemic immune responses after H-FIRE treatment, analyze tumor biopsies, blood immune cells, and cytokines before and after treatment, and determine whether a single H-FIRE treatment can stimulate a meaningful anti-tumor immune response.
L157: ### Eligibility - Inclusion Criteria
L158: 
L159: Before enrollment, standard diagnostic testing is required, including:
L160: 
L161:   * Complete physical examination
L162:   * Bloodwork (CBC and chemistry)
L163:   * Urinalysis
L164:   * Contrast CT scan of the chest and abdomen (under anesthesia or sedation)
L165:   * Ultrasound-guided liver tumor biopsy
L166: 
L167: Dogs may qualify if:
L168:   * One or more liver tumors are identified
L169:   * Tumors are amenable to surgical resection
L170:   * The dog is a suitable candidate for anesthesia and surgery
L171:   * The owner has reviewed all standard-of-care options and elects to participate
L172: ### Eligibility - Exclusion Criteria
L173: 
L174: Dogs are not eligible if they have:
L175: 
L176:   * Severe systemic illness that prevents safe anesthesia or surgery
L177:   * Coagulation disorders that prevent biopsy or electroporation
L178:   * Medical conditions that substantially increase anesthetic risk
L179:   * Owner declines surgical tumor removal following H-FIRE
L180: ### What Participation Involves
L181: 
L182: H-FIRE Treatment:
L183: 
L184: The H-FIRE procedure is performed under general anesthesia and guided by ultrasound. One or more needle electrodes are placed through a 1-2 mm skin opening into the tumor. Electrical pulses are delivered in microsecond bursts. Total treatment time is typically under 30 minutes.
L185: 
L186: Surgery (5-7 Days Later):
L187: 
L188: Surgical removal of the liver tumor under general anesthesia with a CT scan obtained immediately before surgery.
L189: 
L190: Follow-Up:
L191: Dogs return at 2 weeks post-surgery for physical examination and suture removal. Additional diagnostics may be performed if medically indicated.
L192: ### Risks and Side Effects
L193: 
L194: H-FIRE is an experimental therapy and is not part of standard veterinary care. Potential risks include fever, tumor inflammation, tumor-site discomfort, systemic inflammation, severe infection, and death. Diagnostic and anesthesia risks include bruising, inflammation, infection, anesthetic reactions, cardiopulmonary complications, and rare death.
L195: ### Potential Benefits
L196: 
L197: Your dog may or may not directly benefit. Potential benefits include partial financial support for treatment, access to a novel tumor-targeted therapy, possible local tumor destruction, possible immune activation, and contribution to research benefiting both dogs and humans.
L198: 
L199: ### Alternatives to Participation
L200: 
L201: Alternatives include surgery alone, palliative medical management, no treatment, or euthanasia when medically appropriate.
L202: ### One-Sentence Financial Summary
L203: 
L204: The study provides a $2,000 surgical credit and covers all H-FIRE, recheck, and post H-FIRE CT costs; owners remain responsible for remaining surgical fees, complications, and unrelated medical care.
L205: ### Costs and Compensation
L206: 
L207: Covered by the Study:
L208: 
L209:   * $2,000 credit toward surgical resection
L210:   * 100% of H-FIRE procedure costs (anesthesia, electrodes, treatment delivery, side-effect management)
L211:   * 100% of post-H-FIRE CT imaging
L212:   * 100% of recheck visit costs
L213: 
L214: Owner Responsibility:
L215: 
L216:   * Remaining surgical costs beyond the $2,000 credit
L217:   * Any medical complications unrelated to H-FIRE therapy
L218:   * Any medical care not required by the study
L219:   * Any unrelated medical expenses
L220: Typical surgical cost at Purdue ranges between $4,000-$8,000 depending on tumor location and surgical complexity.
L221: ### Voluntary Participation and Withdrawal
L222: 
L223: Participation is entirely voluntary. Owners may withdraw their dog from the study at any time without affecting access to standard care. Dogs may also be withdrawn for medical or safety reasons. Samples collected before withdrawal may still be used unless the owner requests otherwise.
L224: ### Confidentiality
L225: 
L226: All study data are confidential. Published results will not include identifying information. Research records are stored securely and accessible only to authorized personnel.
L227: 
L228: ### Trial Status
L229: 
L230: Currently Enrolling

L241: ## HIFU Osteosarcoma Study
L242: ### Principal Investigators
L243: 
L244:   * Dr. Nick Dervisis, Associate Professor, Oncology
L245:   * Dr. Michael Childress, Professor, Comparative Oncology
L246: ### Study Overview
L247: 
L248: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological impact of High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU) for dogs newly diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma (OSA). Osteosarcoma is an aggressive primary bone cancer with a high risk of lung metastasis even with current standard treatments. HIFU is a noninvasive, image-guided technology that uses focuses ultrasound energy to generate heat and destroy targeted tumor tissue without skin incision.
L249: ### Purpose of the Study
L250: 
L251: The goal of this study is to determine whether HIFU can safely modulate the tumor microenvironment, stimulate immune responses, and enhance future combinations with immune-based therapies. Advanced functional imaging and molecular analysis will be used to characterize biological effects before and after HIFU treatment.
L252: ### Eligibility - Inclusion Criteria
L253: 
L254:   * At least 1 year old and >8 kg (18 lb)
L255:   * Confirmed appendicular osteosarcoma
L256:   * No evidence of metastatic disease
L257:   * Suitable acoustic window for HIFU
L258:   * Healthy enough for anesthesia and surgery
L259:   * No chemotherapy within 3 weeks and no corticosteroids within 2 weeks
L260:   * No other serious life-limiting disease
L261:   * Relatively normal organ function
L262: ### Eligibility - Exclusion Criteria
L263: 
L264:   * Other cancer types or metastatic osteosarcoma
L265:   * No acoustic access to the tumor for HIFU
L266:   * Other life-limiting illness
L267:   * Poor overall performance status (VCOG _ 2)
L268: ### What Participation Involves
L269: Screening and baseline evaluation include physical examination, bloodwork, CT imaging, biopsy, and ultrasound assessment of tumor accessibility. On Day 0, dogs undergo functional imaging (Dynamic Contrast CT and Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy). On Day 1, partial tumor ablation is performed using HIFU under general anesthesia. Five to seven days later, repeat imaging and sample collection are performed. Between Days 6-8, standard-of-care limb amputation is performed.
L270: After recovery, dogs receive adjuvant carboplatin chemotherapy.
L271: ### Follow-Up
L272: 
L273: After surgery and recovery (approximately 14 days), dogs begin standard carboplatin chemotherapy. Following the completion of chemotherapy, dogs return every 3 months for re-staging, ideally with CT imaging of the chest and abdomen. Owners are asked to notify the oncology team of any changes in their pet's health.
L274: ### Risks
L275: 
L276: HIFU risks may include skin irritation, swelling, increased pain at the treatment site, unknown risk of bone fracture, systemic inflammation, abscess formation, and in rare cases, death. Diagnostic procedures may cause bruising, inflammation, or infection. General anesthesia carries small risks, including rare fatal complications.
L277: Chemotherapy is not experimental but may cause vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, and decreased blood cell counts. Dogs will be monitored carefully and supported as needed.
L278: ### Potential Benefits
L279: 
L280: Your dog may or may not directly benefit from participation. Potential benefits include access to a novel noninvasive tumor ablation therapy, advanced imaging and molecular tumor analysis, partial financial assistance for surgery, and contribution to research benefiting both dogs and humans.
L281: 
L282: ### Alternatives
L283: 
L284: Alternatives to participation include standard limb amputation followed by chemotherapy alone, palliative care, no treatment, or euthanasia when medically appropriate.
L285: ### One-Sentence Financial Summary
L286: 
L287: The study fully covers all HIFU and functional imaging costs, provides up to $2,600 toward surgical amputation, and covers chemotherapy recheck visits, while owners remain responsible for remaining surgery, chemotherapy, and surgery-related complication costs.
L288: ### Costs and Compensation
L289: 
L290: Covered by the Study:
L291: 
L292:   * 100% of all HIFU-related costs (general anesthesia, samples, treatment, management of HIFU-related side effects)
L293:   * 100% of all functional imaging (Dynamic Contrast CT and Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy)
L294:   * Up to $2,600 toward surgical amputation
L295:   * Free recheck visits during chemotherapy
L296: 
L297: Owner Responsibility:
L298:   * Initial diagnostics and staging
L299:   * Remaining surgical costs beyond the $2,600 credit
L300:   * Chemotherapy drug administration (carboplatin)
L301:   * Any medical complications related to surgery
L302:   * Any unrelated medical care
L303: 
L304: Total expected cost of surgery and chemotherapy typically ranges from $4,000-$6,000 depending on dog size, limb affected, tumor location, and surgical complexity.
L305: ### Voluntary Participation and Withdrawal
L306: 
L307: Participation is voluntary. Owners may withdraw at any time. Withdrawing does not affect access to care. Samples already collected may still be used unless the owner requests otherwise.
L308: 
L309: ### Confidentiality
L310: 
L311: All information collected during this study is confidential. Research records are secured, and published results will not contain personally identifying information.
L312:

L314: 
L315: Currently Enrolling
